findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Hom.lean:79-88 `@[simp] lemma pairing ... (f : Hom P Q) : Q.pairing (f.indexEquiv i) (f.indexEquiv j) = P.pairing i j`. The proof body at EquivInvariance.lean:76-77 mentions `g` only via `g.toHom.pairing`.
findings.fix: State it for `(f : RootPairing.Hom P P₂)`: `P₂.pairingIn ℤ (f.indexEquiv i) (f.indexEquiv j) = P.pairingIn ℤ i j`. Uses written `g.indexEquiv` for an `Equiv` still elaborate to `Hom.indexEquiv g.toHom`, so the call sites in Symmetry.lean are unchanged.
findings.issue: `pairingIn_indexEquiv` takes `g : P.Equiv P₂`, but the proof uses only `FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective` and `g.toHom.pairing`; bijectivity of the weight/coweight maps is unused. The ℤ-valued statement should sit at the same level as the Mathlib lemma it wraps.

findings.evidence: Proof at lines 86-89 is `P₂.root.injective` + `Hom.root_weightMap_apply P P₂ _ g.toHom` + `map_neg`; `Defs.lean:85` gives `root : ι ↪ M`. The remaining lemmas (`mem_range_root_weightMap_iff`, the two `_iff` transport lemmas, `linearIndependent_root_indexEquiv_iff`, the chain lemmas) genuinely need injective `weightMap`, so `Equiv` is right for those.
findings.fix: State for `(f : RootPairing.Hom P P₂)`. Then update the module docstring title/blurb, which currently claims the file is about equivalences.
findings.issue: Same defect: `indexEquiv_neg` assumes `g : P.Equiv P₂`, but its proof uses only injectivity of `P₂.root` (which is an embedding for every root pairing) and linearity of the weight map via `Hom.root_weightMap_apply` — no bijectivity.

findings.evidence: Symmetry.lean:330-338: `noncomputable def geckLieAut ... := geckLieEquiv g τ hτ` and `theorem geckLieAut_apply ... := geckLieEquiv_apply g τ hτ x`.
findings.fix: Delete the `Automorphism` section (`geckLieAut`, `geckLieAut_apply`); downstream callers use `geckLieEquiv g τ hτ` with `P₂ := P`, `b₂ := b`, which already has type `lieAlgebra b ≃ₗ⁅R⁆ lieAlgebra b`. If a genuinely new automorphism-only fact is wanted (e.g. multiplicativity in `g`), add that instead of an alias.
findings.issue: `geckLieAut` is `geckLieEquiv g τ hτ` at `P₂ := P`, `b₂ := b` — same type, same term, no added structure (it is not packaged as a `LieAut`-valued group hom or anything else). `geckLieAut_apply` (line 335) likewise restates `geckLieEquiv_apply`, and because `geckLieAut` is a `def` the two are separate `@[simp]` lemmas for the same fact. Special-case duplication of API already proved in general.

findings.evidence: The proof (lines 150-154) is `coe_reindexAlgEquiv`, `reindex_apply`, `Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv`, `ext; simp [Function.comp_def]` — nothing root-pairing-specific; and all root-pairing instances are `omit`ted at lines 141-142.
findings.fix: Prove the general matrix lemma `LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R ε.symm (A *ᵥ v) = reindexAlgEquiv R R ε A *ᵥ LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R ε.symm v` for `ε : n ≃ m` (`[Fintype n] [Fintype m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq m]`) in a Matrix file, and obtain the current statement by specialising `ε := geckIndexEquiv g τ`.
findings.issue: `geckModuleEquiv_mulVec` is a statement about an arbitrary matrix and an arbitrary index equivalence — the root pairings `P`, `P₂`, the bases `b`, `b₂`, `g` and `τ` enter only through `geckIndexEquiv g τ` and play no role. It is stated one level too low.

summary: Two EquivInvariance lemmas assume a full `RootPairing.Equiv` where their proofs only use `Hom`-level facts, `geckLieAut`/`geckLieAut_apply` are contentless special cases of `geckLieEquiv`/`geckLieEquiv_apply`, and `geckModuleEquiv_mulVec` is a pure matrix fact stated with inert root-pairing hypotheses.
